God's hatred is directed toward the human person in two registers: (1) toward wickedness and those whose inner disposition is hatred of him (groups 3595, 3596 — 33 verses). Psa 5:5: "you hate all evildoers." Psa 11:5: "his soul hates the wicked." Deu 7:10: "repays to their face those who hate him, by destroying them." (2) The divine-to-human movement is consistently a response to what the human has done or become. Hos 9:15: "there I began to hate them. Because of the wickedness of their deeds" — the divine hatred is responsive to human choices.

Minimally and only in reactive/judicial form. Deu 32:19: "the Lord saw it and spurned them (na.ats), because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters." Lam 2:6: "the Lord has...spurned (na.ats) king and priest." These are judicial responses to Israel's prior contempt of him. God's movement toward the human in M06-B is not the extension of contempt as a disposition but the execution of a judicial response.

Yes, extensively. Group 252-003 (9 verses): Psa 106:40: "he abhorred his heritage." Amo 6:8: "I abhor the pride of Jacob." Psa 5:6: "the Lord abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man." God's abhorrence is sustained and serious — a real inner-being response to persistent covenant violation and corruption. The basis is always the accumulation of moral failure, never arbitrary.

Only in the descriptive sense of Isa 13:9 (the severity of divine judgment described using the cruelty term). The divine movement toward the human in M06-D is consistently the removal and judgment of the ruthless (Isa 29:20, 13:11) and the deliverance of those who suffer under them (Isa 49:25, Jer 15:21, 20:11). God is the answer to cruelty, not its practitioner toward the human person.

God acts to remove reproach from the human person (the dominant divine movement), and also imposes it as covenantal judgment (secondary, judicial). Removal: Gen 30:23 — "God has taken away my reproach." Jos 5:9 — "today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." Isa 25:8 — "the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth." Imposition: Eze 5:14 — "I will make you a desolation and an object of reproach among the nations." Even the imposition is reversible (Eze 36:15).

Yes — Exo 23:22: "I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries." God takes up the adversary posture on the human person's behalf. This is not God extending enmity toward the human but God positioning himself as adversary to those who threaten the human. God's movement toward the person is as advocate and contender.

God acts as the judge of malice, not as its subject or practitioner. Eze 25:6-7: "because you have clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the malice within your soul against the land of Israel, therefore, behold, I will stretch out my hand against you." God's movement toward the human person who exercises malice is judicial response.

The God-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced directional axis across all seven sub-groups. This is the primary relational interface in M05. The cluster's characteristics are all first and most fully evidenced as divine dispositions toward the human person — before they are human dispositions toward others.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — God's righteousness reaches the human person through: (1) proclamation (the declared standard that confronts the conscience, A1-005/006); (2) the Messiah (A1-007: God's righteousness incarnated and extended to humanity through Christ); (3) covenant faithfulness (A1-003: God's righteousness expressed toward his covenant people as reliability, keeping promises, betrothing in righteousness); (4) saving acts (A1-004: deliverance, vindication, restoration — all flowing from God's righteousness toward the person in need).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — righteousness is given to the person by God: "born of him" (1Jo 2:29, VSG M26-A2-014); "the righteousness of God" in the person (2Cor 5:21, VSG M26-A2-008); credited to Abraham (Gen 15:6, VSG 3410-001). God extends righteousness to the human person as a gift received by faith — this is the primary mode of the God-to-human interface in M26.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — justification is definitionally a God-to-human act. "God who justifies" (Rom 4:5, VSG 3194-001); "justified by his grace" (Tit 3:7). Justification flows exclusively from God toward the person — the human person cannot justify themselves.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — God executes avenging justice toward wrongdoers: "he has judged the great prostitute... and has avenged on her the blood of his servants" (Rev 19:2, VSG 944-002). God also executes justice toward the wronged through response to their cry (Luk 18:7–8, VSG 945-001: "he will give justice to them speedily").

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — God condemns: "he condemned sin in the flesh" (Rom 8:3, VSG 4846-002); condemnation falls on those who disobey the gospel (2Th 1:9, VSG 949-001). God's condemnation is directed toward sin and toward those who reject righteousness.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — God reckons: "it was counted to him as righteousness" (Rom 4:3–11, VSG 3410-001). The divine reckoning of faith as righteousness is the most explicitly God-to-human operation in F.

**[CLUSTER — T4.1]** E. God's righteousness operates toward the human person in every mode: as gift (A2, C), as proclamation (A1-005), as incarnation through the Messiah (A1-007), as saving deliverance (A1-004), as reckoning of faith (F), as avenging justice (D), and as condemnation of sin and unrighteousness (E). The God-to-human interface in M26 is comprehensive and operates in multiple directional modes.

Two modes of divine engagement with M46-A. First, divine commission of inner closure as judicial act: Isa 6:10 (God commands the making-fat of the heart as judgment on a people already resistant). Second, divine address to the inner-closed: Rev 3:17-18 (Christ addresses the Laodicean church with diagnosis and counsel — "I counsel you to buy from me gold refined by fire"). God both produces inner closure as judgment and addresses it with redemptive counsel.

M46-C has rich evidence of God toward the human person. God makes rich (1Sa 2:7), God's blessing makes rich without sorrow (Pro 10:22), God gives wealth and the power to enjoy it (Ecc 5:19), God provides richly (plousiōs) all things for enjoyment (1Ti 6:17). The divine provision of material goods is a recurring theme in M46-C — God is active in the material domain as the giver of wealth.

M46-D has the definitive God-to-human movement: 2Cor 8:9 (Christ who was rich voluntarily became poor for human enrichment). God's provision is also evidenced in the peace of God guarding hearts and minds (Phil 4:7 — the context of learned contentment); and in God bestowing riches on all who call on him (Rom 10:12 — plouteō as divine act toward the invoking human).

M46-B shows the divine judgment on wealth that produces hardness: Jam 5:1-5 (judgment pronounced on those who accumulated unjustly) and Rev 18 (judgment on Babylon's commercial wealth-system). God's response to M46-B's patterns is judicial.

God is uniquely active across the entire cluster — more so than in most other programme clusters examined to date.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, explicitly and repeatedly. God exults over his people with gladness and loud singing (Zep 3:17 — su.s and gil_verb); rejoices in doing Israel good with all his heart and soul (Jer 32:41 — su.s); will rejoice over restored Zion as a bridegroom over a bride (Isa 62:5 — su.s); will rejoice in Jerusalem and be glad in his people (Isa 65:19 — gil_verb and su.s); takes delight in prospering the restored (Deu 30:9 — su.s). The God-to-human direction is one of the most strongly evidenced directions in the corpus.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, extensively and across multiple registers: (1) **God produces joy in the heart** — Psa 4:7 ("you have put more joy in my heart"); Ezr 6:22 ("the Lord had made them joyful"); Ecc 5:20 ("God keeps him occupied with joy in his heart"); 2Ch 20:27 ("the Lord had made them rejoice over their enemies"); (2) **God gives joy as a gift** — Ecc 2:26 ("God has given wisdom and knowledge and joy" to the one who pleases him); Psa 126:3 ("the Lord has done great things for us; we are glad"); (3) **God fills with joy** — Rom 15:13 ("may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing"); Act 13:52 ("filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit"); (4) **God's own joy over his people** — Luk 15:7, 10 (joy in heaven and before the angels over the repentant sinner); Zep 3:17 (God rejoicing over his people with gladness); Jer 32:41 (God rejoicing over Israel in doing good); (5) **Jesus' joy given to disciples** — Joh 15:11 ("my joy may be in you"); Joh 17:13 ("that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves"); Mat 25:21, 23 ("enter into the joy of your master").

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes, in two registers: (1) **Spirit-produced agalliao** — the Holy Spirit is the primary agent producing Suffering-Joy in the human person: Luk 10:21 (Jesus' agalliao is "in the Holy Spirit"); 1Th 1:6 (adjacent — "joy of the Holy Spirit" received amid affliction); Act 13:52 (adjacent — "filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit"). The Spirit is God-toward-the-human-person in the constitutional dimension; (2) **Eschatological promise as the ground** — the "joy set before him" (Heb 12:2), "your reward is great in heaven" (Mat 5:12), and "when his glory is revealed" (1Pe 4:13) are God's word-of-promise operating as the cognitive-eschatological ground that the Spirit works through to produce Suffering-Joy. God-toward-the-human-person operates through both Spirit and word.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, extensively and at the most fundamental level. (1) **M04-L-VCG-01 — divine character goodness**: God is the originating subject of the evaluative-goodness faculty — Gen 1:4–31 (God sees and declares good); Gen 2:18 (God identifies the not-good and remedies it); Psa 25:8 ("good and upright is the Lord"); Psa 86:5 ("you are good and forgiving"); Psa 100:5; 106:1; 107:1; 118:1, 29; 135:3; 136:1 (the ki-tov formulas — God's goodness declared as the ground for praise); Nah 1:7 ("The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble"); Lam 3:25 ("The Lord is good to those who wait for him"); Psa 145:9 ("The Lord is good to all"); (2) **M04-O-VCG-04 — covenantal promise and good hand**: God's good hand enabling Ezra's journey (Ezr 7:9; 8:18); God's good hand enabling Nehemiah's petition (Neh 2:8); God's good hand as the testimony motivating communal action (Neh 2:18); God's good promises fulfilled (Jos 21:45; Jer 29:10; 33:14; Num 10:29); (3) **M04-O-VCG-03 — God producing wellbeing**: Ezr 6:22 ("the Lord had made them joyful"); 2Ch 20:27 ("the Lord had made them rejoice" — adjacent); Psa 112:5 ("it is well with the man who deals generously" — God's moral order producing wellbeing for the righteous).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — God's Delight directed toward the human person is the most extensively documented God-to-human inner-being movement in M04. Six modes: (1) **Rescue and exaltation from Delight** — Psa 18:19 / 2Sa 22:20 ("he rescued me, because he delighted in me"); Psa 37:23 ("the steps of a man are established by the Lord, when he delights in his way"); 1Ki 10:9; 2Ch 9:8 ("delighted in you and set you on the throne"); Num 14:8 ("if the Lord delights in us, he will bring us into this land"); (2) **Relational naming from Delight** — Isa 62:4 ("you shall be called My Delight Is in Her, for the Lord delights in you, and your land shall be married") — God's Delight toward Zion producing a new covenantal identity; (3) **Parental cherishing** — Jer 31:20 ("Ephraim my darling child" — sha.a.shu.im persisting through rebuke, God's heart yearning) — God-to-human Delight as the most tender relational form; (4) **Restoration from Delight** — Deu 30:9 ("the Lord will again take delight in prospering you") — divine Delight as the engine of national restoration; (5) **Wisdom as God's delight** — Pro 8:30–31 — God's daily sha.a.shu.im in Wisdom, and through Wisdom in the children of man — the creative-relational Delight that constitutes the human-divine relationship from the beginning; (6) **Trinitarian Delight** — Mat 3:17; 12:18; 17:5; Mar 1:11; Luk 3:22; Col 1:19; 2Pe 1:17 — the Father's eudokeo directed toward the Son, which is the archetype of all divine-to-human Delight.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, in three primary God-to-human registers: (1) **God's pleasant character extended toward the community** — Psa 90:17 ("let the favor/pleasantness [no.am] of the Lord our God be upon us") — divine pleasantness as a character-quality that God extends toward his people; (2) **Divine beauty received by the worshiper** — Psa 27:4 ("to gaze upon the beauty [no.am] of the Lord") — God's own beauty as the object that the worshiper receives as Pleasure; God extends his beauty toward the seeking person; (3) **Divine river of delights** — Psa 36:8 ("you give them drink from the river of your delights [ed.nah]") — God lavishly supplying delight from his own inexhaustible source toward those who feast in his house; (4) **Eschatological acceptance as pleasing aroma** — Eze 20:41 ("as a pleasing aroma I will accept you") — God extending his receptive Pleasure toward restored Israel as a future-oriented covenantal gift; (5) **Pleasures forevermore** — Psa 16:11 ("at your right hand are pleasures forevermore") — God as the permanent source of pleasure in his own presence.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes, in two primary God-to-human directions: (1) **God performing wonders toward Israel** — the dominant VCG-01 pattern throughout: God's marvellous deeds are the divine acts directed toward the human community that produce Wonder as the response; Exo 3:20 (wonders done in Egypt); Exo 34:10 (marvels "before all your people"); Psa 31:21 ("he has wondrously shown his steadfast love to me when I was in a besieged city") — divine wonders extended as saving acts toward the person in distress; Joe 2:26 ("the Lord your God, who has dealt wondrously with you") — wonder-acts as the mode of divine engagement with the covenant community; (2) **God opening the eyes to behold wonders** — Psa 119:18 ("open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law") — the petition implies God extends the capacity for Wonder as a gift; the ability to perceive the wondrous in Scripture is itself a God-to-human act.

**[CLUSTER]** E — God-to-human operation is evidenced for all seven characteristics, but with a clear hierarchy of breadth: (1) **Delight (Char 4)** is the most extensively documented God-to-human characteristic in the cluster — six distinct divine registers (rescue from Delight, relational naming from Delight, parental cherishing as Delight, restoration from Delight, trinitarian Delight, and creative-Delight in Wisdom before creation). No other characteristic in M04 has as many distinct divine-to-human registers; (2) **Joy (Char 2)** is the second most extensively evidenced — God produces Joy in the heart (Psa 4:7), makes them joyful (Ezr 6:22), fills with Joy through the Spirit (Gal 5:22), and sends Christ's own Joy into the disciples (Joh 15:11); (3) **Gladness (Char 3)** operates from God primarily through his character (M04-L-VCG-01 — divine goodness as the archetype of all evaluative gladness) and through his providential acts (good hand, fulfilled promises); (4) **Wonder (Char 6)** — the entire VCG-01 corpus (61 verses) is God performing wonders toward Israel; God also opens the eyes to perceive wonders (Psa 119:18); (5) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7)** operates from God primarily through the Holy Spirit (Luk 10:21; 1Th 1:6) — the most constitutionally immediate divine-to-human Suffering-Joy; (6) **Pleasure (Char 5)** and **Exultation (Char 1)** are less God-to-human in primary orientation (they are more human-toward-God), but God's exultation over his people (Zep 3:17; Jer 32:41) and God's pleasant beauty (Psa 27:4's no.am) confirm God-to-human operation in both.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, in a specific and distinctive way. God deploys shame as a judicial verdict and as a moral instrument directed at human persons. The M07-B evidence documents God "putting enemies to shame" (Psa 44:7; 53:5; 86:17; Zec 10:5), exposing idol-makers to shame (Isa 44:9-11; 45:16), and placing shame on those who opposed his servant (Isa 41:11; 42:17). This is God using shame as a tool of judgment — it moves from God toward the person as a consequence of their action against God or his people. More remarkably, God also deploys shame as a restorative instrument toward his own people: the commands in Eze 16:52; Eze 36:32; Eze 43:10 — "be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel" — are divine invocations of shame directed at his covenant people as the gateway to renewal. God extends shame toward the human person both as judgment (on enemies) and as corrective mercy (on his own people).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Extensively evidenced in VCG-03. God extends CHAR-2 to the proud as a judicial act: "your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down" (2Sa 22:28); "the Lord God of hosts will lop the boughs with terrifying power" (Isa 10:33); "I will change their glory into shame" (Hos 4:7). God also extends CHAR-2 redemptively through the mortal body's state (1Cor 15:43) — the dishonored mortal condition is God-ordained as the seed-state for the glorified body. The judicial basis is moral cause (pride, idolatry, opposition to God's servant); the redemptive basis is eschatological purpose.

**[CHAR-3]** E — God extends CHAR-3 in the structural-assignment mode (VCG-02): the potter's sovereign assignment of vessels for dishonorable use (Rom 9:21) is God's prerogative in the creation and governance of persons. The basis is God's authority over his own creation; the content is the objective assignment of standing according to God's sovereign purpose.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — God is the standard against which CHAR-4's evaluative operation works ("in the sight of God," 2Cor 4:2). God's giving over of persons to dishonorable passions (Rom 1:24; 1:26) — "God gave them up" — shows God as the agent who permits the VCG-02 moral disorder as a consequence of idolatry. This is not God extending shamefulness but God releasing the person into the shamefulness their own choices have generated.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — God acts against CHAR-5 rather than extending it: 1Cor 1:28 — God choosing the despised to nullify things that are — is God's counter-movement against the world's contempt-verdicts. God's sovereign reversal of CHAR-5 is the theological foundation for why the recipient of contempt need not be defined by the contempt-verdict. God does not extend contempt-producing-shame toward persons; he extends the reversal of contempt and the vindication of the despised.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — God confirms and validates CHAR-6: Gen 20:6 (contextually) — God's response to Abimelech's appeal to innocence is to confirm it and grant protection. God is the authoritative validator of the innocence-claim: whether CHAR-6 is present is not merely a self-assessment but a reality confirmed or denied by God. God also reveals the incapacity for innocence (Hos 8:5) — the divine question "how long will they be incapable of innocence?" reveals that God tracks the moral condition of CHAR-6 and names its loss.

---
